findings.title: The package's own top-level module docstring is not a map of the module any more
locations: src/GBGCodingTools.jl:26-45: "The module is a map; every part is documented at its home. The command line and its configuration: … The engines: …"
findings.description: GBGCodingTools's module docstring explicitly bills itself as the map of the whole package ("The module is a map; every part is documented at its home", RULE.DOC.MODULE_MAP) and then names exactly nine things: main, Config, makedocs, TestHarness, Reflection, Witnesses, the scan-engine trio, TreeHash, HtmlWalker and consolidate. The module's own include list (lines 55-86) names 29 files, and the map gives no linked one-liner — not even a bare mention — for Sync (the managed-file renderer), Doctor, Ledger, RoundFiles, Git, Schema, Seed, Recall, Preflight, Rounds, Passes (the whole round-lifecycle: open, bank, grade, close — arguably the tool's central mechanism), Init, Demote, Hunt, Audit, Fleet, Bump, Release or Selftest. A cold reader of the map has no way to learn any of this machinery exists. RULE.DOC.CURRENT: "a summary that names only a subset of what the code now provides is stale even if literally true."
findings.resolution_hint: Add at least a linked one-liner per operation family the omitted files own (e.g. Preflight/Rounds/Passes — the round lifecycle; Sync — the managed-file renderer; Doctor — the health check; Ledger — the exemption reader) to the map, the way the engines section already covers TestHarness/Reflection/Witnesses.

findings.title: apply_ledger's docstring overstates when a wildcard ledger entry disables a scan
locations: src/Scan.jl:344-345: "with target `*` disables the scan (every hit exempted, `disabled = true`)"
src/Scan.jl:356: `any(e -> e["target"] == "*" && !haskey(e, "match"), scan_entries) && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)`
findings.description: The docstring says a scope = "scan" entry with target = "*" always disables the scan. The code only disables it when that entry ALSO carries no match table (!haskey(e, "match")); a target = "*" entry that does carry a match table falls through to the per-hit loop below and is applied like any other exemption (only hits whose file/symbol/arg satisfy the match are exempted, the rest are kept). match alongside target = "*" is a legal combination under schema/exemptions.schema.json (nothing forbids it), so this is a reachable, not merely theoretical, case the docstring gets wrong. (The scope = "policy" disable check just above it, lines 351-352, has no such match guard and is described correctly.)
findings.resolution_hint: Qualify the scan-scope clause: "…with target `*` and no `match` table disables the scan…", distinguishing it from a wildcard entry that does carry match, which is instead evaluated per hit.

findings.title: TestHarness's module map omits its own exported counting helper
locations: src/TestHarness.jl:10-18: the module docstring's "the element-traffic audit ([`TestHarness.CountingArray`](@ref), [`TestHarness.Traffic`](@ref), [`TestHarness.audit`](@ref))"
src/TestHarness.jl:26: `export @alloc_below, CountingArray, Traffic, counting, audit, run_regressions, gate`
findings.description: counting is one of only seven names TestHarness exports, and it has its own docstring (line 133), but the module docstring's map of the element-traffic audit lists CountingArray, Traffic and audit and never mentions counting — the constructor a user actually calls to wrap an array before auditing it.
findings.resolution_hint: Add [`TestHarness.counting`](@ref) to the element-traffic-audit bullet, e.g. "([`TestHarness.counting`](@ref), [`TestHarness.CountingArray`](@ref), [`TestHarness.Traffic`](@ref), [`TestHarness.audit`](@ref))".
